notes:

The 1206-1209 shape gives the Latins Bithynia and Mysia before they held them (Pegai only, 1205-1211); the 1210-1219 shape adds a lobe to 22.9E/42.4N (Melnik, Strumica, Prosek) that was Alexius Slav's vassal lordship or Bulgarian; the 1220-1226 shape should end in 1224/25 (Poimanenon, cession of Asia, Epirote Thrace: new keyframe 1225); the 1227-1235 and 1236-1249 shapes keep the Asian block and inland Thrace long after Nicaea (1225, 1235) and Epirus/Bulgaria (1225-1230) took them and are marked wrong with Constantinople-centred corrections. Infobox areas (179,000 km2 in 1204, 206,000 in 1209) count the vassal states (Thessalonica, Athens, Achaea, Negroponte, the Archipelago), which Cliopatria draws separately; 47,000 (1228) and 14,000 (1260) are the comparable figures for the direct domain, against Cliopatria's 55,305 and 2,997.

Vassals recorded in the ledger (rule 4): Kingdom of Thessalonica 1204-1224; Principality of Achaea 1209-1261 (nominally to Viterbo 1267); Duchy of Athens 1209-1261; the triarchs of Negroponte 1209-1261 (Venice the effective overlord); Duchy of the Archipelago 1210-1248; David Komnenos' Paphlagonia 1206-1212 (nominal, confidence 1); Alexius Slav's Melnik-Rhodope lordship 1209-1230 (confidence 1, no page loaded). The Latin duchy of Philippopolis (Renier of Trit, 1204-c. 1230) is treated as direct land. Epirus' Michael I submitted to Henry in 1209/10 (Latin Empire page) but the relation is not drawn.

Gaps and disagreements: fall of Constantinople 24 July (Baldwin II page), 24/25 July (main page) or 25 July 1261 (Reconquest infobox); Poimanenon 1223 or 1224; the Treaty of Nymphaeum 1212 (Treadgold) or December 1214; the Adrianople sequence 1225 (Nicaea) - 1227 (Epirus) rests on the Vatatzes page alone; Tzurulum's loss (1247) and Philippopolis' end (c. 1230) are not on the pages opened. Pages that would not load: 'Latin Duchy of Philippopolis', 'Byzantine-Latin wars'. The byzantine-empire row has no shapes 1227-1278, so the restored empire of 1261-1278 is carried by the Nicaean row; the byzantine-empire dossier needs new keyframes 1261-1278 (flagged in the report).

Gazetteer names used as coordinates or polygons because the gazetteer lacks them: Pegai, Cyzicus, Gallipoli, Tzurulum, Vizye, Kalamos, Lesbos, Chios, Samos, Kos, Lemnos; Philippopolis and the Rhodopes are drawn as Bulgarian oblasts; Adrianople around Edirne; Serres around Seres.
